paper_title: Employing Equivalent Circuit Models to Study the Performance of Selenium-Based Solar Cells with Polymers as Hole Transport Layers

qa_pairs.question: What are the champion performance parameters of a selenium solar cell using P5NH as the hole transport layer?
qa_pairs.answer: The P5NH-based selenium solar cell achieved a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 4.3%. This performance is characterized by a short-circuit current (Jsc) of 8.99 mA cm⁻², an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 858.3 mV, and a fill factor of 56.0%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Employing Equivalent Circuit Models to Study the Performance of Selenium-Based Solar Cells with Polymers as Hole Transport Layers

qa_pairs.question: Describe the device architecture and materials sequence used in the selenium solar cells studied.
qa_pairs.answer: The devices utilize a conventional n-i-p sandwiched structure. The specific sequence of materials is Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) / Tin oxide (SnO2) / Tellurium (Te) / Selenium (Se) / Hole Transport Layer (HTL) / Silver (Ag).
qa_pairs.source_title: Employing Equivalent Circuit Models to Study the Performance of Selenium-Based Solar Cells with Polymers as Hole Transport Layers

qa_pairs.question: How do the energy levels of P5NH and P25NH facilitate efficient charge carrier management in selenium solar cells?
qa_pairs.answer: The HOMO levels of P5NH (-5.4 eV) and P25NH (-5.18 eV) are shallower than the valence band maximum of the selenium film (-5.64 eV), which allows for efficient hole extraction without energy barriers. Simultaneously, their LUMO levels (-3.4 eV for P5NH and -3.5 eV for P25NH) are significantly higher than the conduction band minimum of selenium (-3.8 eV), creating an energy barrier that blocks electron diffusion into the HTL and reduces recombination.
qa_pairs.source_title: Employing Equivalent Circuit Models to Study the Performance of Selenium-Based Solar Cells with Polymers as Hole Transport Layers

qa_pairs.question: What effect does the application of P5NH and P25NH HTLs have on the surface morphology of the selenium absorber layer?
qa_pairs.answer: According to atomic force microscopy (AFM), the application of these polymer HTLs smoothens the interface. The root mean square (RMS) roughness of the selenium surface is reduced from 29.629 nm to 20.591 nm when using P5NH and to 21.171 nm when using P25NH, leading to improved electrical contact.
qa_pairs.source_title: Employing Equivalent Circuit Models to Study the Performance of Selenium-Based Solar Cells with Polymers as Hole Transport Layers

qa_pairs.question: Based on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), which polymer HTL is more effective at suppressing surface recombination in selenium solar cells?
qa_pairs.answer: P5NH is more effective at suppressing surface recombination. EIS analysis revealed that P5NH-based solar cells exhibit a recombination resistance (R2) that is an order of magnitude higher than that of P25NH-based devices.
qa_pairs.source_title: Employing Equivalent Circuit Models to Study the Performance of Selenium-Based Solar Cells with Polymers as Hole Transport Layers

qa_pairs.question: Why does P5NH demonstrate superior performance compared to P25NH in selenium solar cells despite both being DPP-based polymers?
qa_pairs.answer: The superior performance of P5NH is primarily attributed to its higher hole mobility of 5.13 × 10⁻² cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹. This higher mobility facilitates more efficient charge transport, leading to smaller recombination losses compared to P25NH-based devices.
qa_pairs.source_title: Employing Equivalent Circuit Models to Study the Performance of Selenium-Based Solar Cells with Polymers as Hole Transport Layers

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of incorporating a discontinuous tellurium (Te) layer in the selenium solar cell fabrication process?
qa_pairs.answer: The discontinuous Te layer serves as an interlayer between the SnO2 and Se layers to improve adhesion. Furthermore, it supports the formation of well-oriented polycrystalline trigonal selenium (t-Se) films during the gradient thermal evaporation and annealing process.
qa_pairs.source_title: Employing Equivalent Circuit Models to Study the Performance of Selenium-Based Solar Cells with Polymers as Hole Transport Layers

qa_pairs.question: How does the dark saturation current density (J0) correlate with the open-circuit voltage (Voc) in P5NH versus P25NH selenium solar cells?
qa_pairs.answer: P5NH-based cells exhibit a much lower dark saturation current density (J0) of 1.74 × 10⁻⁵ mA cm⁻² compared to 1.07 × 10⁻³ mA cm⁻² for P25NH-based cells. This lower leakage current (J0) in P5NH devices correlates directly with their significantly higher observed open-circuit voltage (858.3 mV vs. 736.3 mV for P25NH).
qa_pairs.source_title: Employing Equivalent Circuit Models to Study the Performance of Selenium-Based Solar Cells with Polymers as Hole Transport Layers
